rules.title: Seattle ban on algorithmic coordinating services
rules.requirement: Prohibits specified algorithmic coordinating services used to set rents in Seattle rental housing. Penalties may reach $7,500 per violation.

coverage.summary: The secondary source states no building, unit-count or landlord-size limits. The cited lawsuits involve Seattle multifamily properties.

rules.effective_date_note: The only source, a law-firm alert, gives 'effective July 2025' (month only). No exact date is available from an official source.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits specified coordinating services; penalties may reach $7,500 per violation
rules.review_note: Supported only by a secondary law-firm alert (Morgan Lewis, Aug. 21, 2026). The ordinance text was not captured. Still to verify from the official ordinance: the exact effective date, the definition of 'coordinating service', covered properties, exemptions and the enforcement mechanism (private versus public). The alert lists the penalty section as 'ch. 7.34.040'. The section-level cite § 7.34.040 is inferred from that. The alert also notes that ordinances of this kind may face challenges to municipal authority and retroactive effect.
rules.source_notes: Law-firm alert. The ordinance is at issue in Nicolas v. Essex Management Corp. and Romano v. UDR Inc. (W.D. Wash.).
